title: RBAC v2 cutover: Emergency admin-bridge, forensic audit preservation, and staged customer opt-in
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose: Execute a minimally disruptive cutover from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 while ensuring emergency admin access, full forensic-grade audit log preservation, and a staged opt-in for customers who require extra validation. This ticket coordinates the temporary admin-bridge service, dual-write reconciliation tooling, SSO mapping dry-run, and communications for customers with strict compliance needs.

Scope:
- Deploy an 'authorization-bridge' sidecar that translates RBAC v1 requests to v2 semantics for emergency admin flows only. The bridge is time-limited and feature-gated.
- Ensure audit logging is immutable and export-ready: enable write-through journaling, checksum headers, and short-term retention on a WORM-like export to object storage for the cutover window.
- Run a dual-write period (v1 -> v2) with a continuous validator that samples and grades differences, emitting SLO violations if divergence crosses thresholds.
- Execute SSO/SAML user mapping dry-runs against production-like data to validate identity mapping rules and group-to-role translations.
- Provide a per-customer opt-in switch to remain on RBAC v1 for up to two weeks post-cutover while capturing necessary telemetry for migration assistance.
- Prepare rollback and emergency de-escalation playbooks, including immediate re-enable of RBAC v1 routing and admin-bridge expansion patterns.

Key technical decisions so far:
- Bridge will enforce an admin-only allowlist using a short TTL admin token and require OPA policy 'escape hatch' approvals.
- Audit logs will be exported to a dedicated s3 bucket with object encryption via KMS and immutable lifecycle TTL for 90 days. Checksums (SHA256) will be calculated server-side and recorded in a signing manifest.
- Dual-write consistency validator will run in streaming mode with an eventual reconciliation job that writes deltas to a dedicated reconciliation index in ElasticSearch for triage.
- SSO mapping dry-run will operate in read-only mode: no role assignments will be written, but mapping outcomes will be recorded in a sandbox namespace.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full deprecation automation of RBAC v1; long-term role schema unification (separate initiative).

Risks:
- Divergence between v1 and v2 semantics for implicit roles may cause permission regressions; mitigation: targeted traffic shadowing and a high-sensitivity alert rule for any 403s from previously-allowed endpoints during canaries.
- Audit export failure during cutover could hinder forensics; mitigation: parallel export targets and health checks with automatic retry/backoff.
- SSO mapping gaps for legacy group claims; mitigation: customer-facing mapping review sessions and manual override paths.

Success criteria (short term):
- Bridge active and gated, with admin token TTL enforced.
- Zero customer-facing authorization regressions for canary cohort (5 customers) across 72 hours.
- Audit export manifests validated (checksums match) for all events produced during the canary window.
- Dual-write validator reports <0.1% divergence for canary cohort and <1% for pilot wave.

Operational contacts and on-call rota: Security Eng: Marcus Li (assignee), Platform SRE: Priya Rao, Product PM: Daniel Ortiz.

Next milestones (dates are target):
- 2026-02-23: Authorization-bridge staging deploy and internal failover test.
- 2026-03-02: Start dual-write validator in passive mode and begin SSO mapping dry-runs.
- 2026-03-08: Canary cutover for 5 low-risk customers with full audit export enabled.
- 2026-03-15: Pilot expansion to 25 customers if canary green.
- 2026-03-20: Finalize roll schedule and customer opt-in windows.

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the audit export manifest format and the reconciliation index schema. Security review must sign off on admin bridge gating token TTL and approval flow before any prod cutover.

acceptance_criteria: Authorization-bridge deployed behind feature flag and can be enabled/disabled by rollout service
Admin emergency token flow implemented with TTL and OPA approval event recorded in audit logs
Audit export completed for the entire canary period with checksum-verified manifests
Dual-write validator running and divergence dashboard available; alerts configured at configured thresholds
SSO mapping dry-run reports produced and sign-off checklist completed for canary customers
Customer opt-in toggle created and validated; opt-in customers remain on RBAC v1 without service impact
